name: Aqua Foam
lede: A water world where the whole surface is foam: teal troughs, white crests, and nothing calm anywhere.
body: Built in Blender as a cube-sphere of 24 tiles, each with its own baked texture, so the surface keeps its detail even up close. Exported in lo and hi versions; this page uses a lighter web cut of the lo file.

name: Arcanum
lede: Grey cloud cover scored with rings of orange sigils, like survey marks left behind on a moon.
body: One baked colour map on a single sphere. The sigil rings sit in the texture itself, so the world reads as a drawing as much as a planet. Exported at 2K, 4K and 8K.

name: Emerald Tide
lede: Shallow green seas braided with bright tidal channels, under a thin drift of cloud.
body: A single baked colour map, tuned so the channels stay legible from orbit and still hold up when you land. Exported at 2K, 4K and 8K.

name: Inferno
lede: A crust of cooling lava split by glowing seams, wrapped in its own layer of heat haze.
body: 24 surface tiles plus a separate six-tile haze shell that glows on its own. The shell is what makes the planet feel hot rather than just orange. Exported at lo, hi and ultra.

name: Nebula
lede: Violet and cobalt bands folding into each other, cut by one bright jet stream across the face.
body: The largest world in the system. One baked colour map on a sphere, lit here by the core so its bands turn with the light. Exported at 2K, 4K and 8K.

name: Terra Nova
lede: Continents, shallow seas and a separate cloud layer. The most ordinary world here, and the hardest to get right.
body: 24 surface tiles and a six-tile cloud shell floating just above them, so weather and ground move as two layers. Exported at lo, hi and ultra.

name: Tempest
lede: A deep blue ocean ringed by cyclone cells, with a second storm layer riding above the surface.
body: Two meshes: the ocean surface and a storm layer that sits just above it. The cyclones are baked into the colour map. Exported at 2K, 4K and 8K.
